title: RichAuto A11 post polish: accept M08 for flood, correct the VFD note and two refusal messages

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

- `coolantCode()` accepts only the exact text `M8` as the flood code. A machine file that gives `M08` is refused with "requires M8, got M08" (`assets/posts/richauto.cps:211-216`). M08 and M8 are the same code. The workaround is to write `M8` in the machine file.
- The header note says `VFD MULTI-SPEED: 8 STEPS ON INPUTS S1-S8` (`richauto.cps:381`). The A11 has three output lines (Y2 to Y4, labelled S1 to S3) that encode 8 speed steps. It does not have 8 inputs.
- The radius compensation refusal says that G41/G42 "is unsupported by RichAuto DSP A11" (`richauto.cps:432`). The A11 code list has G41 and G42. The manuals show no D word and no tool radius table.
- The tapping refusal says that G84 "is unsupported by RichAuto DSP A11" (`richauto.cps:613`). The A11 code list has G84. A standard A11 has no spindle encoder input and no reverse spindle output.

## Expected

- The post accepts `M8` and `M08`. It compares the number, not the text.
- The note says that 3 output lines encode 8 speed steps.
- The two refusals say that this post does not support the function, and give the cause (no D word or radius table; no spindle encoder or reverse output). The refusal behaviour does not change.

## Evidence

Main `8937e684d`, at the lines above. Sources: the RichAuto DSP A11 user manual (G-code list and VFD multi-speed wiring).

Found by the post audit against the RichAuto manuals (#4130).

## Done means

- A test pins a machine with flood `mCode` `M08` that posts flood coolant as `M8`.
- The changed note is in the goldens. The changed messages are in the refusal tests.
